verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own change-management features for flags. A change history logs changes to flags and other resources, flag changes can go through approval requests, and change history can roll a flag back to a previous version. Flag targeting is also where its automation lives (scheduled changes, progressive and guarded rollouts). However, the evidence never shows versioning, review, or rollback applied to the automation definitions themselves, such as schedules, triggers, or rollout plans. missing for 10: explicit versioning, review, and rollback of the automations themselves (scheduled changes, triggers, guarded or progressive rollouts), evidence that approvals cover automated changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly keeps a running log of changes made to feature flags and other resources in each environment.
You can also use the change history to [roll back](/docs/home/releases/version-restore) a flag to a previous version.
